text.title: THE SCAEAN GATE
text.intro: The ninth year of the war. The Achaeans press hard against the city, and Diomedes rages on the plain like a river in flood. Hector, son of Priam, has come back from the fighting to bid the women pray, and to find his wife.
text.death_text: The Achaeans drag his armour from him before the gate. On the tower a woman has seen it.
text.end_text:
Hector stripped the armour of Achilles from the body of Patroclus and put it on. He would wear it to his death. By the ships, a man who had sworn not to fight heard the news and rose.

After Iliad 6.237-529 and 16.684-867.

objectives.find: Find Andromache at the Scaean Gate
objectives.sortie: Go out through the gate to the men at the oak
objectives.hold: Hold the ground before the gate
objectives.myrmidons_sub: The man in the armour of Achilles

andromache_1: Hector. Your own strength will be the death of you. Have you no pity for your little son, or for me, who will soon be your widow?
andromache_2: Achilles killed my father, and my seven brothers in a single day. You are father and mother and brother to me now, and you are my husband.
andromache_3: Stay here on the tower. Set the army by the wild fig tree, where the wall is easiest to climb.
hector_1: All this weighs on me too. But I could not face the men of Troy, nor the women with their trailing robes, if I shrank from the fighting like a coward.
hector_2: I know it in my heart. The day will come when holy Ilios shall fall, and Priam, and the people of Priam of the good ash spear.
child: You reach for your son. The child cries out and hides his face against his nurse, afraid of the bronze and of the horsehair crest nodding above it.
laugh: You laugh, and Andromache laughs with you. You set the shining helmet on the ground and take the boy in your arms.
prayer: Zeus, and all you gods: let this boy be as I am, first among the Trojans. And let men say of him one day, as he comes home from war, 'He is better by far than his father.'
fate: Do not grieve too much. No man will send me down to Hades before my time. And no one born has ever escaped his fate, coward or brave.
parting: She goes toward the house, turning often to look back, and weeping.
paris_1: Brother. I have kept you waiting.
hector_3: Come. We will make it good hereafter, if Zeus ever lets us drive the Achaeans from Troy.
rally: Trojans, Lycians, Dardanians who fight hand to hand: be men, my friends! Remember your fury!
wave_1: They are coming up from the river! Shields!
wave_2: More of them, on the left! Hold the line by the oak!
achilles_cry: A cry runs down the Achaean line: 'Achilles! Achilles has come out!' The armour is his. The man inside it is Patroclus.
patroclus_1: Myrmidons! To the wall! Today we take the city of Priam!
apollo_1: Give way, Patroclus. It is not fated that the city of the proud Trojans fall to your spear, nor to the spear of Achilles, who is a better man than you.
apollo_2: Three times he sets his foot on the angle of the wall. Three times something throws him back.
apollo_strike: A mist comes down across the fighting. Out of it something strikes Patroclus between the shoulders. His eyes swim. The helmet of Achilles rolls in the dust.
euphorbus: Euphorbus, son of Panthous, drives a spear into his back and runs. Patroclus staggers toward his own men.
hector_4: Patroclus! You thought to sack our city and carry our women to your ships. Fool.
patroclus_2: Boast while you can, Hector. Zeus and Apollo gave you this. They beat me, not you. I would have killed twenty such as you.
patroclus_3: And you will not live long yourself. Death and strong fate are standing beside you already, at the hands of Achilles.
hector_5: Why prophesy my death, Patroclus? Who knows but Achilles may be struck first, by my spear?
